claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA contains FCC and ordered B2 phases.
The initial alloy has a nanolamellar microstructure.
The initial FCC phase is disordered while the B2 phase is ordered.
Aging at 400–700 °C for 1–100 hours evolves LCOs in B2 and sharpens FCC/B2 phase boundaries.
Coarsening and ordering of LCOs forms coherent, high-strength B2 precipitates that impede dislocation glide.
During aging, B2 changes from a disordered or weakly ordered state into a highly ordered L10 or B2 superlattice.
Increasing order in B2 raises the Peierls barrier for dislocation motion.
Chemically sharp FCC/B2 boundaries lacking misfit dislocations inhibit dislocation transmission.
Inhibited glide and transmission confine dislocations to B2, causing pile-ups, stress concentrations, and crack initiation.
At higher aging temperatures, LCOs dissolve or B2 partially disorders.
High-temperature disordering lowers the Peierls barrier, enables cross-slip or phase-boundary transmission, and restores ductility.
Aging at 500–600 °C produces elongation to failure below 10%.
Aging above 700 °C restores elongation to failure above 20%.
Embrittlement occurs when the B2 ordering parameter is 0.6–0.8 and before significant decomposition or coarsening.
The brittle regime will exhibit increased B2 ordering and reduced dislocation density inside B2 domains.
The as-cast or solution-treated baseline has greater than 30% elongation and no significant B2 ordering.
Prior evidence shows retention of ordered B2 in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 during cryo-rolling and thus provides limited evidence of B2 stability.
The cited prior evidence supports the proposed dislocation behavior in increasingly ordered B2 domains.
Absence of C, O, or S segregation at FCC/B2 interfaces, together with a correlation between B2 order and ductility loss, falsifies a grain-boundary embrittlement mechanism.
Observation of impurity segregation at FCC/B2 phase boundaries supports a grain-boundary mechanism.

contradictions.description: The initial state identifies B2 as ordered, whereas the baseline says there is no significant B2 ordering and the proposed transition begins from disordered or weakly ordered B2.
The hypothesis attributes embrittlement partly to coarsening, but the boundary defines embrittlement as occurring before significant coarsening.
The specified aging range ends at 700 °C, while recovery is predicted only above 700 °C, placing the recovery branch outside the stated intervention range.
